methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Late Stage → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $52M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Kinova Robotics is a late-stage private robotics company founded by Charles Deguire and Louis-Joseph L'Ecuyer that has raised $51.6M to date. The target operates within Robotics & Manufacturing, a sector encompassing one public comparable (277810.KQ) and eight private peers including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable triangulation approach. Using total capital raised ($51.6M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical for late-stage to next-stage advancement yields an implied value of $62M. This reflects the expected value accretion associated with Kinova's progression within its funding lifecycle. The peer-median method is not applicable due to insufficient comparable datapoints at matching or adjacent stages within the Robotics & Manufacturing sector; while ten same-sector peers exist, none satisfy the narrow filtering criteria (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar valuation tier) required for reliable benchmarking.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $53M (low) to $71M (high), centered on $62M. This range reflects the limitations of a single-method triangulation. Key uncertainties include the absence of stage-matched comparables for cross-validation and reliance on a generic multiplier rather than sector-specific progression rates. Refinement would benefit from closer stage-matched peers or revenue/profitability metrics to anchor valuation to operational performance rather than funding history alone.
